findings.summary: Blender is a free and open-source 3D creation suite used for modeling, animation, rendering, and video editing. It originated as an internal tool at the Dutch studio NeoGeo in 1994, was released as shareware in 1998, and became open-source in 2002 after a community-funded campaign. The project transitioned to the Blender Foundation and community development, removing its integrated game engine in version 2.80 to focus on other workflows.

mechanisms.title: Community-driven open-source development
mechanisms.explanation: After Blender became open-source in 2002, development continued through the Blender Foundation and community contributors, including over 50 full-time and freelance developers at the Blender Institute.

mechanisms.title: Integrated creative pipeline features
mechanisms.explanation: Blender provides a unified application for 3D modeling, animation, rendering, compositing, motion tracking, and video editing, replacing the need for separate tools in a typical production pipeline.
